what_happened: The job changed the queue drain so that re-reads of items marked "needs-accepting" no longer count toward the drain job limit. The verifier rejected it at the final verdict. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet. That criterion says the same test, run against the old `run_job` counter, would stop with `Stop::JobLimit` before `b` runs, so the test fails without the fix. There was one major finding: behavior criterion 2 is unmet because its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). No failed checks are listed. The fix itself is not reported as wrong. The gap is missing proof that the test fails without the fix, backed by a command that was actually run.
cause: Nothing prompts the producer to run and record a command for each behavior criterion before it finishes. This criterion needs a "fails without the fix" demonstration: run the new test against the old counter and see it fail. Nothing in the producer's flow supplies or asks for that run, and the evidence rule (D43) is enforced only by the verifier at the end. There is also no cheap repair step for missing evidence, so rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the producer's report is not in the stored fields.
prevention: Add a check that runs before the verifier. For each behavior criterion, it requires a recorded command and its output in the producer's report. For "fails without the fix" criteria, Athena itself should run the new tests against the pre-change source, for example by stashing the production diff and running the named test, and record that the test fails. If any behavior criterion has no recorded run, the producer is sent back for one repair round instead of the job being rejected.
proposed_request: Make the drain job limit ignore needs-accepting re-reads, so they do not count toward the limit. Add a test in which the job limit is 1 and item `a` is re-read as needs-accepting before item `b` runs. The test must show that `b` still lands and that the drain does not stop with `Stop::JobLimit`. Before finishing, run that test against the old counter, with the production change temporarily reverted, and record the command and its failing output. Then run the same test with the fix and record that it passes. Run the full gate (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo test --workspace`) and record those commands too. For every behavior criterion in the report, cite the command that ran and its result. Add a CHANGELOG entry. Do not change any governance files.
